description:
FOUND s460ao while shipping #890's runtime decline.  PRE-EXISTING and on BOTH
emission paths; it is NOT caused by the decline, which only made it visible by
letting the program run to the `++` instead of dying at the write.

PERL: `++` and `--` are AUTOGENERATED from a `+`/`-` overload handler when the
class does not overload them directly (and `fallback` allows it), and the
result is whatever the handler returns — normally another OBJECT.

    package NumOvl;
    use overload '0+' => sub { $_[0]{v} },
                 '""' => sub { 'N(' . $_[0]{v} . ')' },
                 '+'  => sub { my ($a,$b)=@_;
                               NumOvl->new($a->{v} + (ref($b) ? $b->{v} : $b)) },
                 fallback => 1;
    sub new { bless { v => $_[1] }, $_[0] }

    my $y = NumOvl->new(5);  $y++;  $y++;
    perl : ref($y) is NumOvl, "$y" is N(7)
    PCL  : ref($y) is '' (a plain number 7) on BOTH paths

PCL numifies instead: `perl-increment` (the boxed `p-post++`/`p-pre++` family)
and `p-incf-raw`/`p-decf-raw` (the raw twins) both compute a NUMBER, so the
object is gone after the first increment.  The same gap exists for the compound
family: `$x += 2` does not run a `+` handler either (`%define-compound-pair`
builds every new value as `(+ (to-number cur) (to-number delta))`).

WHAT s460ao DID FIX HERE, and why it is only half: `perl-increment` did
`(unbox val)` FIRST and then numified the bare payload, so the class was gone
before `to-number` could dispatch `0+` at all — the boxed path answered the
blessed hash's address-ish 1 and the raw path answered 5, i.e. ONE program with
TWO answers (`$y++;$y++;print $y+0` gave 3 under PCL_OPT=none and 7 by
default).  The `0+` handler is now asked on the BOX, so both paths agree at 7.
Agreement is all that was bought: 7 is still not perl's answer.

SHAPE OF A FIX (unmeasured).  There is ONE new-value builder for the compound
family (`%define-compound-pair`, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) and one for incdec
(`perl-increment`), so this is two places, not a family sweep.  The candidate
is to route the new value through the OVERLOAD-AWARE op (`p-+` etc.) rather
than `(+ (to-number …) (to-number …))`, with perl's autogeneration rules:
`++` prefers a `++` handler, else `+` with a 1, else numify.

MEASURE FIRST (the s335 rule, and this one has teeth): `p-incf-raw` is the
`intloop+=` and `cfor` bench rows' inner loop — 0.0186 s / 5M iterations at
s460ao, 0.28x perl.  `p-+` has an inline numeric fast path, so the cost MAY be
nil, but a bench A/B on intloop+=/intloop=/cfor is the gate, not an argument.
If it costs the rows, the arm can be conditional on the operand being a box
(the raw fast path then pays one type test, which is what %pcl-raw-freeze-
unsafe-p already costs at the write).

BAR: the probe above matches perl on both paths; the four counting-loop bench
rows do not regress; corpus-diff (no emission change expected — this is
runtime-only); full sweep; the `#890` block in Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t stays
green and gains a row for the object-preserving `++`.

SHIPPED s461ar (agent AR, round 18) -- the AUTOGENERATION half.  perl's
REFUSAL half is deliberately NOT shipped and is task #934 with its measured
matrix.

WHAT LANDED, all in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:
  * %p-incdec-overload (val op-str gen-op) -> (values new-value applied-p).
    The class's own `++`/`--` handler first, else AUTOGENERATE from `+`/`-`
    with a 1, keeping whatever the handler returns.  Two values because a
    handler may legally return undef.
  * perl-increment consults it FIRST; the `0+` arm below it is now reached only
    when the class overloads neither `++` nor `+`.
  * perl-decrement is NEW and is the one reading of the `--` new value:
    p-pre-- and p-post-- had FOUR copies of `(1- (to-number PLACE))` between
    them and none could see an object.  perl has no magical string decrement,
    so the non-overload arm stays numeric.
  * %p-incdec-old: POSTFIX ++/-- hand back a COPY OF THE REFERENCE for a
    blessed box.  perl's postfix on an overloaded object with no `=` copy
    constructor yields the SAME referent; unboxing dropped the class, so
    `my $r = $obj++` came back a bare hash (ref '' , "$r" of 1).
  * %compound-arith-form + %p-compound-+-slow / ---slow for `+=`/`-=`.

THE GUARD'S SHAPE IS THE INTERESTING PART, and the bench harness could NOT
settle it -- a sibling agent had four cores busy and `perl(s)` itself swung
2.5x between runs, giving a "cfor +10 %" that did not reproduce.  Five
candidates were timed INSIDE the runtime core instead (the two loop bodies
written out by hand, best-of-5, three rounds), against the form being replaced
(`(+ (to-number cur) (to-number delta))`, cfor = raw+raw, fe = raw+BOXED):

                                              cfor      fe
    the form being replaced                  0.0280   0.0500
    (a) delegate to p-+ outright                       +49 %
    (b) blessed test inline                   -4 %     +15 %
    (c) numberp test first, then (b)          -3 %     +23 %
    (d) as (c), slow half out of line          0 %     +49 %
    (e) SHIPPED: *p-any-overload-registered*
        first, then (b)                       -4 %      +5 %

*p-any-overload-registered* is a new one-way defvar set by p-register-overloads
(which %p-overload-import routes through, so both entry points are covered).
It is the PROGRAM-level question -- NIL in every program that never says
`use overload` -- and one memory load.  *p-overload-table*'s COUNT would answer
the same thing, but hash-table-count is an out-of-line call, which is the
measurement already recorded in %p-no-overload-possible-p's comment.

THE RAW TWIN NEEDS THE GUARD, measured not assumed: `my $s = 0; $s += $obj;`
emits `(p-incf-raw $s $o)` with an OVERLOADED delta and the slot then HOLDS the
object, so neither operand of a raw `+=` is provably a number.

BARS: the 12-row + 6-row probe tables byte-identical to perl 5.40.3 on BOTH
emission paths (default and PCL_OPT=none); gate 191/6461; full perl-tests sweep
GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18342 (+0), drops 5 = census; companion op/ + re/
legs; guard Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t +2 rows (31 -> 33), inverse-verified on a
33a71c9 worktree.  The four counting-loop bench rows do not regress (see the
table above; bench-exec under load agrees within its noise).
subject: ++/-- and += on an overloaded object numify instead of autogenerating from the + handler -- perl keeps an OBJECT, PCL keeps a number (both paths)
